## 1. Purpose

This procedure describes the collection of vertical depth profiles of
water quality parameters (temperature, dissolved oxygen, pH,
conductivity, turbidity, and chlorophyll fluorescence) in lakes,
reservoirs, and deep ponds. Depth profiling characterizes thermal
stratification, the location and extent of the thermocline and
oxycline, and vertical gradients in water chemistry that control
nutrient cycling, habitat availability, and water treatment operations
[@wetzel2001; @kalff2002].


## 2. Scope

- **Applies to:** Vertical profiling from boats, docks, or platforms
  in lentic water bodies (lakes, reservoirs, ponds) and slow-moving
  deep river pools. Covers both manual sonde profiles and Secchi depth
  measurements.
- **Does not apply to:** Continuous deployed sonde monitoring (see
  future SOP); horizontal spatial surveys; stream cross-section water
  quality (see [SOP-F200](SOP-F200-eureka-manta2.qmd) for general
  sonde operation); bathymetric mapping
- **Location:** All EA Program lake and reservoir field sites


## 3. Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                              |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------|
| PI / Field Lead   | Approve profiling plan, coordinate boat access and permits |
| Trained Personnel | Calibrate sonde, perform profiling per this SOP |
| New Students      | Complete training and boat safety orientation before participating |


## 4. Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Drowning:** All lake work involves drowning risk. Personal
  flotation devices (PFDs) are mandatory for all personnel on boats,
  docks, and platforms.
- **Weather:** Lightning, high winds, and sudden storms pose serious
  hazards on open water. Abort profiling if thunderstorms are within
  10 miles or winds exceed safe boating conditions for the vessel.
- **Sun exposure:** Extended time on open water increases UV exposure
  and heat stress.
- **Equipment:** Heavy sonde and cable assemblies can cause hand and
  back injuries when deployed over the side of a boat.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Personal flotation device (PFD) -- worn at all times on the water
- [ ] Closed-toed shoes with non-slip soles
- [ ] Nitrile gloves (when handling calibration solutions)
- [ ] Sun protection (hat, sunscreen, sunglasses)

### Emergency Procedures

Refer to [SOP-F001 Field Safety](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd). All
boat occupants must know the location of PFDs, throwable flotation
devices, and communication equipment (VHF radio or charged cell
phone). If a person falls overboard, deploy the throwable device
immediately and maneuver the boat to the person.


## 5. Equipment and Materials

| Item                                  | Notes                          |
|:--------------------------------------|:-------------------------------|
| Eureka Manta2 multiprobe or equivalent sonde | Calibrated per [SOP-F200](SOP-F200-eureka-manta2.qmd) |
| Sonde cable (length sufficient for maximum expected depth) | Graduated at 0.5 m or 1 m intervals |
| Secchi disk and graduated line        | Per [SOP-F207](SOP-F207-secchi-disk.qmd) |
| Depth sounder or weighted line        | For measuring total water depth at the profiling station |
| Boat, canoe, kayak, or dock access    | Appropriate to site conditions |
| Anchor(s) or tie-off lines            | To hold the boat stationary during profiling |
| GPS unit                              | For recording station coordinates per [SOP-F006](SOP-F006-gps-site-navigation.qmd) |
| Field notebook and profiling data sheet | Waterproof (Rite in the Rain); see Appendix A |
| Camera                                | For photo-documenting site and weather conditions |
| Water sample bottles and cooler       | If discrete-depth water samples are collected alongside the profile |


## 6. Procedure

### 6.1 Pre-Field Preparation

1. Calibrate the sonde per
   [SOP-F200 Eureka Manta2](SOP-F200-eureka-manta2.qmd) before
   departing for the field
2. Verify that the sonde cable is marked at depth intervals (0.5 m or
   1 m). If using a direct-read cable, confirm depth readings against
   a tape measure.
3. Check weather forecast; postpone if thunderstorms are likely or
   sustained winds exceed the vessel's safe operating threshold
4. Review the profiling station coordinates and planned depth intervals

### 6.2 Station Setup

1. Navigate to the profiling station (typically the deepest point of
   the lake or a fixed monitoring location)
2. Record GPS coordinates, date, time, weather conditions (sky cover,
   wind speed and direction, air temperature), and total water depth
3. Anchor or tie off the boat to minimize drift during the profile
4. Perform the Secchi disk measurement per
   [SOP-F207](SOP-F207-secchi-disk.qmd)

### 6.3 Sonde Deployment and Profile Collection

1. Lower the sonde to 0.5 m below the surface. Allow at least
   60 seconds for the sensors to equilibrate (longer for optical DO
   in cold water).
2. Record all parameters (temperature, DO, pH, conductivity,
   turbidity, chlorophyll) at that depth. If the sonde is logging
   internally, note the time and depth; if reading from the handheld
   display, record values on the data sheet.
3. Lower the sonde to the next depth increment (typically 0.5 m in
   the epilimnion and through the thermocline; 1 m increments are
   acceptable in deep hypolimnetic water where parameters change
   slowly).
4. At each depth, allow 30--60 seconds for sensor equilibration before
   recording.
5. Continue to within 0.5 m of the bottom. Do not allow the sonde to
   contact the sediment (stirs up sediment and can foul sensors).
6. After the deepest reading, raise the sonde steadily to the surface.
   If time permits, record an ascending profile for comparison.

::: {.callout-tip}
In productive lakes, the most rapid changes in temperature and DO
occur at the thermocline and oxycline. When you detect these
transitions, switch to 0.5 m or even 0.25 m intervals to resolve
the gradient.
:::

### 6.4 Discrete-Depth Water Sampling (Optional)

If the study design requires water samples at specific depths (e.g.,
epilimnion, metalimnion, hypolimnion):

1. Use a Van Dorn or Kemmerer bottle lowered to the target depth
2. Trip the sampler and raise to the surface
3. Dispense into pre-labeled sample bottles per
   [SOP-F300](SOP-F300-surface-water-sampling.qmd) preservation
   requirements
4. Record the collection depth and time for each sample

### 6.5 Post-Profiling

1. Rinse the sonde sensors with deionized water
2. Replace the sonde in its calibration/storage cup with storage
   solution (especially the pH sensor)
3. Download logged data or scan the data sheet for completeness
4. Confirm that GPS coordinates, Secchi depth, total depth, and all
   profile readings are recorded


## 7. Data Interpretation

A typical stratified lake profile shows three zones:

| Zone          | Characteristics                                        |
|:--------------|:-------------------------------------------------------|
| Epilimnion    | Warm, well-mixed surface layer; high DO, uniform temperature |
| Metalimnion (thermocline) | Rapid temperature decrease with depth (at least 1 C per meter) |
| Hypolimnion   | Cold, dense bottom layer; may be anoxic in productive lakes |

::: {.callout-note}
Not all lakes stratify. Shallow, wind-exposed, or polymictic lakes may
be fully mixed during some or all seasons. Record whether stratification
is present and the depths of the thermocline boundaries.
:::


## 8. Quality Control

- Calibrate the sonde on the day of profiling; record calibration
  results on the calibration log
- Allow adequate sensor equilibration time at each depth (minimum
  30 seconds; 60 seconds at the first depth and near the thermocline)
- Record an ascending profile periodically to check for sensor drift
  during the profile
- Verify depth markings on the cable against a tape measure at least
  once per season
- If the sonde includes an internal depth (pressure) sensor, compare
  cable-marked depth to the sensor depth at several points; discrepancies
  greater than 0.3 m require investigation
- For long-term monitoring, profile at the same station, same time of
  day (within 2 hours), and same depth intervals for comparability

## 11. Training Record

Before performing lake profiling independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP, [SOP-F001](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd), and
   [SOP-F200](SOP-F200-eureka-manta2.qmd) in full
2. Complete boat safety orientation (PFD use, boat handling, man-
   overboard procedures) for the vessel type used at the site
3. Observe a trained operator perform a complete depth profile
   including sonde calibration, Secchi measurement, and data recording
4. Perform a supervised profile and demonstrate proper sensor
   equilibration timing and depth-interval decisions at the
   thermocline
5. Be signed off by the PI or field lead
